claims.text: Segments: the ascending aorta, the aortic arch and the descending aorta.
claims.quote: The aorta consists of the ascending aorta, the aortic arch, and the descending aorta

claims.text: Ascending aorta: rises about 5 cm and ends at the sternal angle.
claims.quote: After exiting the heart, the ascending aorta moves in a superior direction for approximately 5 cm and ends at the sternal angle.

claims.text: Aortic arch: ends at the disk between the fourth and fifth thoracic vertebrae.
claims.quote: The aortic arch descends toward the inferior portions of the body and ends at the level of the intervertebral disk between the fourth and fifth thoracic vertebrae.

claims.text: Thoracic vs abdominal: the aorta is the thoracic aorta above the diaphragm and the abdominal aorta below it.
claims.quote: Superior to the diaphragm, the aorta is called the thoracic aorta, and inferior to the diaphragm, it is called the abdominal aorta.

claims.text: Thoracic aorta: from T5 to the diaphragm at T12.
claims.quote: The thoracic aorta begins at the level of vertebra T5 and continues through to the diaphragm at the level of T12

claims.text: Bifurcation: the abdominal aorta divides into the two common iliac arteries at the fourth lumbar vertebra.
claims.quote: The abdominal aorta terminates when it bifurcates into the two common iliac arteries at the level of the fourth lumbar vertebra.

claims.text: Pulmonary trunk: carries blood from the right ventricle and divides into the two pulmonary arteries.
claims.quote: Blood exiting from the right ventricle flows into the pulmonary trunk, which bifurcates into the two pulmonary arteries.

claims.text: Venae cavae: most systemic blood returns through the superior or inferior vena cava.
claims.quote: Most of the blood flows into either the superior vena cava or inferior vena cava.
